title: Self-taught playing and pre-war records in Bordeaux
summary: No real teacher, lip trouble, improvement from daily playing with Luter; before the war he knew Armstrong and Bix only from scarce records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Not really. Not really. How did you learn jazz? A friend who had a teacher, he tried to teach me a little, but it was not very good. I had years of trouble with my lips and... I was not professional too. I made a sketch and painting at that time. It was just for the few years I played with God Luther, I made improvements because I play every day at that time.
Did you hear many American musicians before World War I? Before World War II?
No. In records, of course, but in person never.
What records did you listen to?
I was in Bordeaux before the war.
Oh yes. What records did you listen to?

Before the war, Armstrong O5, some Bigs by the Meck, and a few white bands. It depends. It was depending on the records that my friends had at that time. In Bordeaux, in a country, in France, before the war, it was difficult to have many records. There were a few records of good jazz in the shop. We had to write to have. It was not encouraging to us.
